punchline: In the Gallup survey Hari cites, only about 13 percent of people said they were engaged in their work.
thirty_sec: Johann Hari points to a Gallup survey in which about 13 percent of people said they were engaged in their work, and to Michael Marmot's Whitehall studies, where lower-ranked civil servants had more stress and more heart attacks. For Hari the key is control, how little say people have over their work. Critics say he selects his evidence.
